claim_1.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of whole blood from the first cohort of volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group; 162 samples in total) collected at days −7, 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28 showed substantial vaccine-induced changes in blood transcript abundance, with the number of responsive genes largest in the pneumococcal vaccine group, smallest in the saline control group, and most changes occurring at days 1 and 7 compared to baseline (days −7 and 0).

sources.quote: Whole-genome transcriptional profiles were generated at each time point from the first cohort of volunteers (n = 6 subjects/ group; 162 samples in total).

It is thus possible to visualize that the number of responsive genes was the largest for the pneumococcal vaccine group and the smallest for the saline control group. Among the different time points, the majority of the changes were seen at days 1 and 7.

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of whole blood from the first cohort of volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group) showed that at day 1 after vaccination (day 1), 17 modules in the influenza vaccine group and 14 modules in the pneumococcal vaccine group were responsive compared to prevaccine levels, whereas later responses were smaller and differed by vaccine.

sources.quote: Out of 62 modules, 17 and 14 passed this threshold at day 1 in the influenza vaccine and pneumococcal vaccine groups, respectively (Figure 2A).

Subsequently, changes in transcript abundance were detected for 3 modules and 1 module at day 7 and 10, respectively, in the pneumococcal vaccine group and for a single module at day 7 and day 21 in the influenza vaccine group (Figure 2A).

claim_3.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of whole blood showed distinct day 1 innate signatures after vaccination, with influenza vaccination inducing interferon/antiviral modules including M1.2, M3.4, and M5.12, and pneumococcal vaccination inducing inflammation-associated modules including M3.2, M4.2, M4.13, M5.1, and M5.7 compared to prevaccine levels.

sources.quote: Three of the four increased modules were associated with antiviral responses (M1.2, M3.4, M5.12, Ingenuity Pathway Analysis enrichment p values)

Six modules were uniquely responsive to the pneumococcal vaccine. Of these, five were modules including genes associated with inflammation (Figure 3B): M3.2 (e.g., CD63, IL-1RN, HMGB2, TLR4, TLR6, TLR8, as well as bcl-6), M4.2 (e.g., CR1, MMP9, TLR5), M4.13 (e.g., CD58, IL-8RA, CXCL1, and IL-1β), and M5.1 (e.g., CCR1, SERPINB8, MAPK1) and M5.7.

claim_4.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of capillary whole blood from an independent cohort (n = 6 subjects per group; 198 samples in total) collected from 168 hours before vaccination through 48 hours after vaccination showed that within hours after influenza vaccination the in vivo signature overlapped with interferon-inducible transcripts induced in vitro by heat-inactivated gram-negative bacteria, heat-inactivated viruses (RSV, influenza), and IFN-γ, whereas the pneumococcal vaccine signature overlapped with signatures induced by heat-inactivated bacteria, LPS, flagellin, PAM3, R837, zymosan, CpG, IFN-γ, and IL-18.

sources.quote: Blood samples were collected via finger stick at hours −168, 0, 1.5, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 24, 36, and 48, for whole-genome transcriptional profiling (198 samples in total) (see Table S5).

The signature elicited within hours following immunization with seasonal influenza vaccine overlapped with transcripts induced by a small set of innate immune stimuli including heat-inactivated gram-negative bacteria, heat-inactivated viruses (RSV, influenza), and IFN-γ.
The pneumococcal vaccine signature overlapped with in vitro signature induced by heat-inactivated bacteria, LPS, flagellin, PAM3, R837, zymosan, CpG, IFN-γ, IL-18.

claim_5.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of capillary whole blood after influenza vaccination showed that significant changes in transcription of genes forming the IFN response module were observed as early as 15 hours after vaccination (day 0.625) and persisted to 48 hours after vaccination (day 2) compared to saline controls and prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Significant changes in the transcription of genes forming IFN response module were observed as early as 15 hr following administration of the vaccine and persisted to 48 hr postvaccination.

claim_6.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of isolated blood leukocyte subsets from a third sequential cohort of healthy subjects (n = 6) before vaccination and 24 hours after influenza vaccination (day 1) showed increased expression of IFN-inducible transcripts in neutrophils and monocytes, identifying these cells as the main contributors to the blood interferon signature compared to CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.

sources.quote: we isolated neutrophils, monocytes, and CD4+ and CD8+ T cells from the blood of study subjects before and 24 hr after the administration of the influenza vaccine (n = 6) in a third sequential cohort of healthy subjects (48 samples in total).
The analysis revealed differences in the levels of expression for IFN-inducible transcripts in neutrophils and in monocytes following influenza vaccination
Thus, administration of the influenza vaccine leads to early type I interferon signature in the blood carried by neutrophils and monocytes.

claim_7.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of whole blood at day 7 after vaccination showed a plasmablast/plasma cell precursor signature (module M4.11) in both vaccine groups, but the response was stronger after pneumococcal vaccination, with 70% of M4.11 transcripts significantly increased versus 35% after influenza vaccination compared to prevaccination levels; this greater pneumococcal response was also present at day 10.

sources.quote: At day 7, the abundance of 35% of the transcripts forming module M4.11 increased significantly in comparison to prevaccination levels in the influenza vaccine group. In the pneumococcal vaccine group, 70% of the M4.11 transcripts were significantly increased.
Furthermore, the amplitude of the plasma cell precursor signature induced by pneumococcal vaccination was significantly greater than that induced by influenza vaccination at both days 7 and 10.

claim_8.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of whole blood showed a spike in circulating plasmablasts at day 7 after influenza vaccination (day 7) and at days 7 and 10 after pneumococcal vaccination (days 7 and 10), with 11-fold and 47-fold increases in absolute plasmablast numbers and mean peak levels of 8.5 cells/uL and 71.7 cells/uL, respectively, compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Plasmablasts were identified by polychromatic flow cytometry in whole blood samples as CD19+lo CD20−CD27+CD38hi plasmablasts and plasma cells.
There, 11-fold and 47-fold increases in the absolute numbers of plasmablasts were observed following vaccination with influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, respectively.

The peak levels reached a mean of 8.5 cells/uL and 71.7 cells/uL in response to influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, respectively. This increase was significant at day 7 following administration of the influenza vaccine and on days 7 and 10 following administration of the pneumococcal vaccine.

claim_9.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of serum showed that CXCL10 (IP-10) increased significantly on day 1 after influenza vaccination (day 1) compared to prevaccination levels.

sources.quote: Furthermore, serum levels of the IFN-inducible chemokine CXCL10 (IP-10) were also found to increase significantly on day 1 after influenza vaccination (p < 0.01; Figure S4).

claim_10.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of serum in the influenza vaccine group showed that antibody levels to the B Brisbane strain were positively correlated with day 7 module M4.11 and increases in HAI titers (r = 0.77), whereas antibodies against the Brisbane H3N2 strain were inversely correlated with M3.3 compared with positive correlations for B Brisbane and Brisbane H1N1 strains.

sources.quote: Some day 7 modules correlating to levels of antibodies were similar to those found in the pneumococcal vaccine group (M4.11 and M4.10) (Figure 7B) with B Brisbane showing the strongest positive correlation with M4.11 and an increase in HAI titers (r = 0.77).
Levels of antibodies against the Brisbane H3N2 strain were inversely correlated with M3.3 (cell cycle) in contrast to a positive correlation for B Brisbane and Brisbane H1N1 strains.

claim_11.claim: commercial immunoassays analysis of serum antibody responses to 14 pneumococcal polysaccharides showed that in the pneumococcal vaccine group the strongest correlations with serology were observed for day 7 modular transcriptional data, with positive correlations for modules M3.3 and M4.11 and negative correlations for inflammation-associated modules M3.2, M4.2, and M4.13.

sources.quote: We explored correlations between day 1 and day 7 modular fingerprints and increases in antibody levels for all available serotypes, combining results from all available subjects for both vaccination groups. The strongest correlations were observed between day 7 modular transcriptional data and serology results in the pneumococcal vaccine group.

The strongest positive correlations were found for modules M3.3 (annotated as cell cycle) and M4.11 (plasma cells) and to a lesser extent M4.10 (B cells), M5.10 and M6.2 (both associated with mitochondrial respiration). Strong negative correlations were observed at the same time point for modules associated with inflammation (M3.2, M4.2, and M4.13).

claim_12.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum showed seroconversion in the majority of subjects at day 28 after vaccination (day 28), and in the influenza vaccine group day 7 module M4.11 correlated with serological response to the B Brisbane vaccine strain (r = 0.77) while day 1 module M5.12 correlated with response to Brisbane H1N1 (r = 0.66).

sources.quote: Neutralizing antibody titers elicited by the different vaccines were determined at days 0 and 28 and demonstrated seroconversion in the majority of subjects

Exploratory analysis of correlation patterns in the influenza vaccine group showed a correlation of day 1 module M5.12 (IFN) expression and serological response to Brisbane H1N1 (r=0.66) and of day 7 M4.11 (plasma cells) with serological response to B Brisbane vaccine strain (r = 0.77).
